items.name: A monic fraction-field factor has integral coefficients
items.statement: Let O be an integrally closed commutative domain and K its fraction field. If monic P∈O[X] has a divisor g∈K[X], there is g′∈O[X] with map(g′)·C(leadingCoeff g)=g. In particular, if g is monic it comes from a unique monic polynomial over O.
items.note: The cited theorem states the displayed leading-coefficient form; its monic specialization uses leadingCoeff g=1 and injectivity of O→K. A DVR is integrally closed. No splitting-field valuation extension is required.

items.name: Norm in a monic polynomial quotient equals the resultant
items.statement: For a commutative ring O, monic R∈O[X] and G∈O[X], Algebra.norm O (AdjoinRoot.mk R G)=R.resultant G R.natDegree G.natDegree. This is the determinant of multiplication by G on the free rank-deg(R) quotient O[X]/(R), even if R is reducible.
items.note: Actual declaration hypotheses and statements read at the pinned commits; containing file bytes match raw GitHub at that commit. Import these declarations, not a new parallel carrier.

items.name: Base change, multiplicativity and monic degree padding for resultants
items.statement: Resultants commute with coefficient ring maps at fixed degree bounds. Res(f₁f₂,g)=Res(f₁,g)Res(f₂,g), with the displayed valid degree bounds; the corresponding product/power formulas hold. For monic f, increasing the valid second degree bound does not change f.resultant g. Over a field, for f≠0, the resultant vanishes exactly when f,g are not coprime.

items.name: A shifted approximate factor detects its multiplicity
items.statement: Let O be a DVR, π a uniformizer, K=Frac(O), R∈O[X] monic of positive degree d and irreducible over K. Write monic P=R^e S in O[X], where R does not divide S in K[X]. For n≥1 let ψ_n∈O[X] be congruent coefficientwise to R+π^n modulo π^(2n). Put c=v(Res(S,R)), finite because R,S are coprime over K. For every n>c, Res(P,ψ_n)≠0 and v(Res(P,ψ_n))=n d e+c, with v(π)=1.

items.name: Monic polynomials are determined by nonzero resultant valuations
items.statement: Let O be a DVR with fraction field K and uniformizer π. Let ι:D→O be a commutative-ring homomorphism surjective modulo every (π^N), N≥1. items.name: DiPippo–Howe lower bound for isogeny classes
items.statement: For every positive integer n and prime power q, the number #O(q,n) of isogeny classes of ordinary n-dimensional abelian varieties over F_q satisfies #O(q,n) > c_4 (c_5 n)^(−2 log 2/log q) (2^n/n!) (r(q) q^(n/2) − n) q^(n(n−1)/4), where c_4 = e^(−3/2), c_5 = 2+√2 and r(q) = φ(q)/q. Hence, with Lemma 2.1 corrected, the logarithm of the number of isogeny classes of g-dimensional abelian varieties over F_q is (1/4)g² log q (1+o(1)) as g→∞, for every fixed q.
items.locator: Remark 2.3; [6] DiPippo–Howe, J. Number Theory 73 (1998), Theorem 1.3 (arXiv:math/9803097v3, p.2)

items.name: A positive involution of a CM field is complex conjugation
items.statement: Let L be a CM field and x ↦ x′ an involution of L that is positive, i.e. Tr_(L/Q)(x x′) > 0 for all x ≠ 0. Then ′ is the complex conjugation of L. In particular, if A is a simple abelian variety with End⁰(A) a CM field, every Rosati involution of A is complex conjugation.
items.locator: §4.5 before Proposition 4.16 and its proof; [19, §21] (Albert's classification)
items.note: The paper uses only this case of Albert's classification. Proof: the fixed field F of ′ has positive definite trace form, so F is totally real; ′ ≠ id because L is not totally real; and the only automorphism of a CM field with totally real fixed field of index 2 is complex conjugation. items.name: Hasse norm theorem for cyclic extensions
items.statement: For a cyclic extension L/K of number fields, x ∈ K^× is a norm from L^× if and only if it is a local norm at every place of K.

items.name: Units that are norms modulo norms of units (Lemmermeyer)
items.statement: Let L/K be a cyclic extension of number fields of prime degree. There is an exact sequence 1 → Am_st(L/K) → Am(L/K) → (E_K ∩ N_(L/K)L^×)/N_(L/K)E_L → 1, where Am(L/K) ⊂ Cl(L) is the group of ambiguous ideal classes and Am_st(L/K) its subgroup of strongly ambiguous classes. In particular (E_K ∩ N L^×)/N E_L is a subquotient of Cl(L) and its order is at most h(L).

items.name: Hasse principle for hermitian forms (Landherr)
items.statement: Let L/K be a quadratic extension of number fields. Two nondegenerate hermitian forms over L (with respect to L/K) that are isometric over L⊗K_v for every place v of K are isometric over L.

items.name: Lang's theorem over finite fields
items.statement: Let G be a smooth connected algebraic group over a finite field k. Then H^1(k, G) = 0. Consequently, for an exact sequence 1 → G′ → G → G″ → 1 of smooth algebraic k-groups with G′ connected, G(k) → G″(k) is surjective.
